title: Write a compaction brief for a 40-turn session
persona: Ananya, running long research sessions with an agent
scenario: Your agent has been working a research task for 40 turns. It is about to hit the context limit and must be compacted into a summary that becomes the new starting context. The session contains: the original brief, 14 sources read (4 of which were later discredited), three abandoned approaches, two decisions you explicitly ratified, a half-finished comparison table, and a running list of open questions. Whatever the summary omits is gone for good.
badPrompt: summarize our conversation so far so we can continue
badOutput: So far we've been researching your topic. We looked at several sources, discussed a few different approaches, and made some decisions about direction. We have an unfinished comparison table and some open questions remaining. Let me know how you'd like to proceed.

hints.title: Rank by what breaks if it's lost
hints.body: Ratified decisions and discredited sources are load-bearing: losing them means re-litigating or re-citing a bad source. Narrative recap is not.

hints.title: Preserve the negatives
hints.body: Abandoned approaches and discredited sources must survive compaction explicitly, or the agent will cheerfully try them again.

checks.tip: Name it as compaction producing a continuation context, not a recap.
Anchor the situation: a 40-turn session at the context limit.
Call out the 4 discredited sources; they must not silently return.
Name the ratified decisions as things that must survive verbatim.
Require abandoned approaches to be carried forward, with why they failed.
Add a negative: no narrative recap, no re-summarising what's already settled.
Make the stakes explicit: this is lossy and one-way.
Require the open questions and next action to survive.
Specify a sectioned structure, not a paragraph.
Ask for decisions and citations verbatim rather than paraphrased.

tipIfLow: Compaction is triage, not summary. Strong version: 'Compact this 40-turn session into a continuation context. Treat it as lossy and one-way: anything you omit is unrecoverable. Preserve verbatim: the original brief, the two decisions I ratified, and the 4 sources found to be discredited, each flagged as do-not-reuse. Preserve with reasons: the three abandoned approaches, so they are not retried. Carry forward the comparison table as-is and the open questions list. Do NOT write a narrative recap of what we discussed. Output under fixed headings: Brief, Ratified decisions, Do-not-reuse, Abandoned approaches, Table state, Open questions, Next action.'
goldPrompt:
You are about to compact this session so we can keep working past the context limit. I'm Ananya; we are 40 turns into a research task.

Treat this as lossy and one-way: anything you leave out is gone for good, so triage by what breaks if it is lost, not by what reads well.

Preserve VERBATIM:
- the original brief
- the two decisions I explicitly ratified
- the 4 sources we found to be discredited, each flagged do-not-reuse with one line on why

Preserve WITH REASONS:
- the three abandoned approaches, each with why it was dropped, so a future turn does not retry them
- the current state of the comparison table, as-is and unfinished
- the open questions list, and the single next action

Do NOT write a narrative recap of our conversation, and do not re-summarise anything already settled — settled things should appear as conclusions, not as discussion.

Output under exactly these headings: Brief · Ratified decisions · Do-not-reuse sources · Abandoned approaches · Table state · Open questions · Next action. If something does not fit a heading and you judge it load-bearing, add it under Carry-forward and say why.
